subject: How to apply non-wear interruptions of 2 mins

messages.author: 38a497f4d21ac289
messages.subject: How to apply non-wear interruptions of 2 mins
parts:
Hi Vincent and team,

I am hoping to process my data as follows using count-based processing (Neishabouri):

Individual summary accelerometry data (minutes of sedentary time, MVPA, VPA, wear-time) obtained at study baseline. These should be derived from the vertical axis, using a 60-s epoch, and non-wear deﬁned as 60 min of consecutive zeroes, allowing for up to 2 min of non-zero interruptions. 

Is there a way in GGIR to apply the 2-min of non-zero interruptions?

Thank you,
Simone

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] How to apply non-wear interruptions of 2 mins
parts:
Hi Simone,

This is not facilitated at the moment.

If you are processing count data it is possible to add this, and I think also sensible if that is what people have used in the literature. Let's discuss when we next meet.

If you are processing raw data converted to counts, e.g. via the NeishabouriCounts parameters in GGIR, then please note that GGIR in that case still uses non-wear detection based on raw data. This far more accurate than any kind of count-based non-wear detection. So, I would advise against using count-based approaches.

Best,

Vincent

Dr. Vincent van Hees | Independent consultant | https://accelting.com/

Hi Vincent,

Thank you for getting back to me. I have now processed these data in ActiLife which gave me those options. I had to match them as this was for a data-harmonization with pre-set processing settings. For future studies I will keep in mind that the non wear is detected using the raw acceleration data and not count-based, thank you!

Kind regards,
Simone
